0.long_answer: Erythroplakia, identified as a red, velvety patch in the oral mucosa, is considered a potentially malignant disorder. A large percentage of these lesions, when biopsied, reveal varying degrees of epithelial dysplasia, carcinoma in situ, or outright invasive carcinoma. Among the types of cancers that may develop from erythroplakia, oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common. OSCC arises from the squamous cells lining the oral cavity, making it the typical cancer associated with erythroplakia.
